newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-CRUZ EARNS NAPOLI CUP DRAW WITH INTER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-CRUZ EARNS NAPOLI CUP DRAW WITH INTER.

text.p: Chilean striker Ivan Zamorano gave Internazionale an early lead in their Italian Cup semifinal first leg match against Napoli on Wednesday.
But Brazilian defender Andre Cruz's goal a few minutes later earned Napoli a deserved 1-1 draw.
The second leg is in Naples on February 26. Bologna and Vicenza play the other semifinal on Thursday.

Zamorano, his form returning after exhausting months travelling between Italy and South America for World Cup qualifiers, set the San Siro stadium celebrating in the sixth minute with a hard, low shot from the right-hand side of the box.
Inter's French midfielder Youri Djorkaeff, playing tirelessly up front, set up the goal.

Inter -- who beat Juventus in the quarter-finals -- dominated much of the match, with 17 shots on goal to Napoli's 11, but the southern team enjoyed more possession and were frequently dangerous on the break.
Cruz netted Napoli's equaliser in the 11th minute with a curling free kick from the edge of the area.
England midfielder Paul Ince had a header from a Djorkaeff corner cleared off the goal-line by a Napoli defender in the 31st minute in an otherwise uneventful first half.
Zamorano came close to scoring a second time early in the second half, goalkeeper Giuseppe Taglialatela making a great reflex save with his outstretched foot as he dived the wrong way.
Inter striker Marco Branca was taken to hospital after the match with a suspected fractured cheekbone.
